title: Six trays.
One closing routine.
metaphor.lead: Picture a TypeScript workbench with six trays of reusable answers. The specialist still does the work. A reusable organizer now owns the trays’ clearing routine. Wiping the trays and finishing the workshop’s shutdown are separate moments.
steps: Six trays keep different kinds of answers apart.
Previously stored answers stop being available immediately.
Only then does the closing call finish or report failure.
metaphor.close: Core supplies the organizer; each TypeScript query service owns one. The backend waits for project cleanup. A fresh work session starts only after refresh succeeds.
metaphor.note: Metaphor: trays are caches, not work queues. Emptying them neither cancels work nor closes access to a cleared tray afterward.

title: “Released.”
Cleanup is still pending.
failure.lead: Suppose project cleanup takes time. In the base, TypeScript clears six caches, starts cleanup, and lets the backend’s release call finish while cleanup is pending. The caller has no completion or failure signal from that cleanup through this call.
steps: Six caches keep different kinds of answers apart.
The scope clears all six caches
Previously stored answers stop being available immediately.
Only then does the release call finish or report failure.
failure.close: Core supplies the scope; each TypeScript query service owns one. The backend waits for project cleanup. A fresh query turn starts only after refresh succeeds.
failure.note: Illustrative failure: the new test supplies delayed, rejecting cleanup. This is not a reported production incident.
